content.content:
# Path App

Path App is a collaborative 3D mapping and navigation project for Hack Western 13. Walk a route with a LiDAR-capable phone, turn the capture into an interactive 3D view, and send someone a link or QR code they can use to find their way.

Visitors can see what a hallway, entrance, or turn looks like before they reach it. Event teams can map rooms and booths, schools and companies can share routes across their campuses, and hikers can share trails they’ve walked. Capture can be handheld or hands-free with a custom 3D-printed wearable phone mount.

## Start here

1. **[Set up your laptop](prompts/team-chat.md)** with the copy-paste commands for your OS.
2. **[Open the live team board](https://github.com/darkprince558/path-app/issues/8)** to see who owns each task and their latest checkpoint. [Create or claim a task](docs/tasks.md) from GitHub or the terminal.
3. **[Start your agent task](prompts/start-task.md)** in its own worktree. Record reusable decisions and findings in the [team notebook](knowledge/README.md).

The [editable roadmap](planning/ROADMAP.md) shows the next milestones. The [planning index](planning/README.md) links the architecture, deployment and demo plans.

Our first milestone is to upload one real scan, share an unlisted link, and open the interactive 3D view on a second phone. Scans can be **Public** (listed for everyone), **Unlisted** (anyone with the link), or **Private** (owner and invited accounts).

| Building | Start with |
| --- | --- |
| Website and 3D viewer | [Arielle’s web workspace](apps/web/README.md) |
| Uploads, sharing and access | [Sam’s API workspace and local commands](services/api/README.md) · [Live deployment plan](docs/deployment.md) |
| Phone capture and export | [Krishna and Anish’s capture workspace](apps/capture/README.md) |
| Shared decisions and development rules | [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) · [Human and coding-agent workflow](AGENTS.md) |
| Working in Claude Code and Codex | [Set up Entire](docs/entire.md) · [Claim a task and launch parallel agents](docs/agent-tasks.md) · [Handoff and review skills](docs/agent-skills.md) |

Run `make check` from the repo root with Python 3.9+ and Make. This checks a synthetic venue and exercises the local upload/share API, including grants and revocation. Start the mock with `make dev-api`. It stores scans for the current process and serves a download page for integration. The guest 3D website, durable backend and device capture are the team's implementation work.

## Hackathon MVP

1. **Capture** a small venue section with a phone’s camera and LiDAR.
2. **Map** the scan into a viewable 3D scene using camera-colored point clouds. Map owners connect walkable waypoints, label destinations, and align contributed sections using manually verified anchors.
3. **Publish** the map and scene assets in the cloud. Map owners approve contributed scans, then share the map via a link or QR code.
4. **Navigate** from a QR-marked starting point to a selected destination. The browser computes a route on the waypoint graph with A* or Dijkstra and draws it over the 3D scene.

Gemini will analyze scan images and return structured suggestions for room numbers, signs, entrances, stairs, and landmarks, along with draft directions. Map owners review suggestions before publishing.

The demo target is one real venue section, two destinations, one route opened from a QR code, and one approved contributed scan appearing in the guest view.

## Team

- **Sam** — Backend APIs, data model, cloud storage, uploads, and event sharing.
- **Krishna and Anish** — Phone capture, scan processing, alignment, and upload integration.
- **Arielle** — Frontend, 3D viewer, route editing, pathfinding, and event experience.

## Prize strategy

Build one demo for **Best Use of Gemini API** and **Most Adventurous**. A first-time visitor chooses an unfamiliar destination, opens a scan and follows a landmark cue grounded in the actual capture. See the [ranked prize plan and 90-second demo](docs/prize-plan.md) and the [Gemini landmark design](docs/gemini-demo.md).

content.content:
# Website

Arielle owns the website: the signed-in home, upload and sharing, and the guest 3D viewer. Build the website here. Start with an upload control, the three visibility choices, a copy-link action and a guest route at `/s/<shareId>`. Display upload, loading and processing failures where they occur.

## Authentication

The existing Next.js backend owns Auth0. React uses `AuthProvider` / `useAuth` and `/api/users/me`, with full-page Sign in / Sign out links. My maps and owner pages require a verified session; Community and authorized guest views work signed out. API requests use same-origin cookies and clear account state on 401. No frontend SDK, tokens or secrets are needed. Run `npm run test:auth:browser` for synthetic browser coverage. See the [production setup and real-login checklist](../../docs/auth0-production.md).

## Automatic routes from approved scans

The existing space and shared-GLB viewers now have **Automatic route** and
**Show NavMesh debug** controls. Verify calibrated metre alignment, enable automatic
routing, then double-click two floor points. Manual graph and saved routes remain
available when the mode is off. See the [full workflow and synthetic tests](../../docs/scan-automatic-routing.md).

Calibration follows validated native capture provenance. To repair an old approved
scan, use **Owner tools → Upload and align scans → Restore validated LiDAR calibration**.

content.text:
Yes, this is possible, and it only needs changes inside the viewer (`apps/web/src/components/SpaceViewer.tsx` and `apps/web/src/lib/scan-surfaces.ts`). I haven't changed anything yet: no branch, no edits. One thing needs your decision first (below).

## What I learned

- **The app:** someone walks a hallway with an iPhone's LiDAR. The capture is fused into a GLB and uploaded through your Next.js API. Guests open it at `/spaces/:id` or `/s/:shareId` in `SpaceViewer` (React Three Fiber). The same three.js objects are used for display, for double-click picking and for building the Recast NavMesh that automatic routing uses.
- **What the scans are:** I opened `paths/Walk 2134 - 34 sections/Hallway.glb`. It's one mesh of 1.37M triangles from "Path Capture depth fusion", with a colour and a normal per vertex. It has no texture, no ARKit surface labels, and a plain material that ignores metal and reflection. The other two walks in `paths/` look similar.
- **Antialiasing is already on.** The viewer sets `antialias: true` with a DPR of 1–2. So the roughness probably isn't jagged edges. A raw depth-fusion mesh tends to look rough because:
  1. **Noisy normals:** small bumps in the fused surface catch the lights, so flat walls and floors look lumpy. This is likely the biggest cause.
  2. **Blotchy colour:** one camera colour per vertex at voxel spacing gives speckle and seams where sections meet.
  3. **Flat depth:** there's no ambient occlusion, so corners and the edges of furniture don't stand out.
  4. **Thin geometry shimmers** while orbiting, which built-in antialiasing doesn't fully fix.
- **The key constraint:** routing, picking and the NavMesh all read this geometry. Every fix should only change how the mesh is drawn, never where its vertices are. That's how `scan-surfaces.ts` already works, and it keeps this task separate from the pathing fix that comes next.

## Proposed approach (viewer only)

1. **Smooth the normals, not the positions:** average each vertex's normal over its neighbours. Walls and floors shade smoothly, and the geometry doesn't change.
2. **Lightly smooth vertex colours** over the same neighbours to reduce speckle.
3. **Add screen-space ambient occlusion and SMAA** through `@react-three/postprocessing`. On phones these would be capped or switched off.
4. **Keep it inside `ScanLook` / `prepareScanSurfaces`.** Steps 1 and 2 run once at load, steps 3–4 are render effects, and there are unit tests plus before/after screenshots.

## The decision I need

**Arielle's open PR #57 (`feature/scan-look-2`) changes the same files.** It changes the lights and tone curve in `SpaceViewer.tsx`, and it hides ceilings using the vertex normals (`normal.y < -0.5`). If I smooth normals on `main`, we'd conflict, and I could change which faces her code treats as ceiling. My suggestion: either wait for #57 to merge, or build on top of her branch and add her as a reviewer, as `AGENTS.md` asks when a shared area changes. Which do you want?

## Other things that would help

- **What "rough" looks like to you:** a screenshot, or a word like lumpy surfaces, speckled colour, jagged edges, holes or floating bits. If you don't have one, I can start the viewer locally, load `Hallway.glb` from `paths/`, and take my own before/after screenshots.
- **Performance target:** which phones the demo has to stay smooth on. Ambient occlusion on 1.37M triangles costs real GPU time, so I'd keep it off on phones unless you say otherwise.
- **Confirming the data stays local:** I'll use the `paths/` walks only to test. They contain real camera frames, so they stay out of commits, PRs and prompts.

I'll do this myself rather than split it across subagents, since it's one focused change.

input.command:
cd /home/sam/Projects/path-app && python3 - <<'EOF'
import json,struct,numpy as np
p="/home/sam/Downloads/2026-11-21 2333 - 3D map.glb"
b=open(p,'rb').read()
n=struct.unpack('<I',b[12:16])[0]
d=json.loads(b[20:20+n]); bin0=20+n+8
print(d['asset'], d.get('extensionsUsed'), 'nodes',d['nodes'])
pr=d['meshes'][0]['primitives'][0]; print(pr['attributes'], len(d['meshes']))
def acc(i):
  a=d['accessors'][i]; bv=d['bufferViews'][a['bufferView']]
  dt={5126:np.float32,5125:np.uint32,5123:np.uint16,5121:np.uint8}[a['componentType']]
  k={'SCALAR':1,'VEC3':3,'VEC4':4}[a['type']]
  off=bin0+bv.get('byteOffset',0)+a.get('byteOffset',0)
  return np.frombuffer(b,dt,a['count']*k,off).reshape(-1,k) if k>1 else np.frombuffer(b,dt,a['count'],off)
P=acc(pr['attributes']['POSITION']); I=acc(pr['indices']).reshape(-1,3)
print('verts',len(P),'tris',len(I)); print('min',P.min(0),'max',P.max(0))
a,bb,c=P[I[:,0]],P[I[:,1]],P[I[:,2]]; N=np.cross(bb-a,c-a); A=np.linalg.norm(N,axis=1)/2
Nn=N/np.maximum(2*A[:,None],1e-12)
for ax,name in enumerate('xyz'):
  up=A[Nn[:,ax]>0.77].sum(); dn=A[Nn[:,ax]<-0.77].sum(); print(f'{name}: +facing area {up:.1f} m2, -facing {dn:.1f} m2')
print('total area',A.sum())
# floor height histogram for upward faces
cy=(a[:,1]+bb[:,1]+c[:,1])/3; m=Nn[:,1]>0.77
h,e=np.histogram(cy[m],bins=20,weights=A[m]); print([ (round(e[i],2),round(h[i],1)) for i in range(20)])
if 'NORMAL' in pr['attributes']:
  VN=acc(pr['attributes']['NORMAL']); fn=VN[I].mean(1); agree=(np.sum(fn*Nn,1)>0).mean(); print('winding agrees with vertex normals:',agree)
EOF

docs/navmesh-navigation.md:28:Input coordinates are right-handed, metres, +Y up, counter-clockwise triangles. Recast cell size is 0.10 m horizontally and 0.05 m vertically. Radius and height are rounded up to voxel counts; maximum step is rounded down. Defaults are radius 0.30 m, height 1.80 m, maximum slope 40°, maximum step 0.20 m. Slope classification, low ceiling filtering, ledge/climb filtering and radius erosion use the triangle geometry. These are conservative rasterized approximations, not a physical accessibility certification.
docs/navmesh-navigation.md:30:Endpoint queries require a polygon directly under the point and at most 0.15 m vertical difference, allowing voxelization error without horizontal snapping. Detour can return a successful partial corridor for disconnected regions; the adapter checks partial, out-of-nodes and buffer statuses and verifies that the last polygon and final route point reach the requested destination. No partial route is drawn. Query arrays, meshes, debug buffers and fixture resources are disposed on rebuild/unmount. Concurrent first builds share initialization so React StrictMode cannot create mismatched WASM instances.
docs/navmesh-navigation.md:32:Empty geometry, nonfinite coordinates, invalid indices, incomplete or degenerate triangles, invalid settings, excessive rasterization bounds, and no walkable output produce errors. The current small-room budget is 600k vertices, 200k triangles, two million horizontal cells, 30 million bounding-volume voxels, and 2048 corridor polygons/route points. Generation is synchronous after initialization and bounded for this fixture. Larger venues need a cancellable Web Worker and tiled generation; this task does not claim large-scan performance. Static mesh extraction rejects skinning, instancing and morph targets until baked. Triangle coverage (including all mesh geometry) determines potential walkability: disconnected wall/box tops can appear green, but cannot be reached from the floor. Unknown or missing geometry must not be treated as surveyed empty space in a real deployment.

**Human owner:** Sam. **Reviewer:** Arielle (automatic routing / NavMesh).

## Problem
On **ACEB Large**, *Show NavMesh debug* showed no floor and no waypoints could be placed. `validate()` in `apps/web/src/lib/navmesh.ts` rejected the scan before Recast ran: its bounds are 48 × 45 × 9.5 m (two storeys plus a stairwell), which is ~41M bounding-volume voxels at 0.10/0.05 m, over the `x*y*z > 30_000_000` cap.

## Fix
Remove the bounding-volume cap. Recast's heightfield is sparse (one entry per horizontal cell plus occupied spans), so cost follows the footprint (2M-cell cap, kept) and triangle count (2M cap, kept), not the empty air in the bounding box. Docs updated.

- Real ACEB Large GLB (local copy, not committed), Node, same `buildNavMesh` path: before, `Geometry exceeds the demo voxel budget`. After, builds in ~0.3 s using about 38 MB more memory. 3,338 debug triangles, walkable on both levels (y ≈ −1.5 and y ≈ 3.0). Points on either floor are pickable.
- New unit test: a 48 × 45 m, 9.5 m tall stacked slab scene. It fails before the fix and passes after.
- `pnpm test` (31 tests), `pnpm build`, `pnpm test:navmesh:browser` (6 passed) and `make check` pass.

## Not fixed here (next task)
Long routes on ACEB still fail with "No complete route connects these regions." The NavMesh splits into about 14 pieces: the lower floor in two at about z = −25, the stairwell in several fragments, and the upper floor. That's the scan-gap problem and gets its own PR.

**Not verified:** on a phone or in the deployed site. A 0.3 s build on desktop Node may be a few times slower on a phone, still on the main thread.

I found it and fixed it: **PR #60** (https://github.com/darkprince558/path-app/pull/60), with Arielle as reviewer.

**Cause:** the floor detection was fine. A size check in `apps/web/src/lib/navmesh.ts` rejected ACEB Large before the NavMesh was ever built. The check capped the scan's bounding box at 30M voxels. ACEB Large is two storeys plus a stairwell, 48 × 45 × 9.5 m, which comes to about 41M. So no NavMesh was built, the debug view had nothing to show, and every double-click was refused.

**Fix:** I removed that cap. It was a guess from the first small-room version, and it doesn't match how Recast uses memory, which scales with surface area rather than the bounding box. The limits on footprint and triangle count are still in place. I found the scan by its database record, read-only, and its byte size matches the copy in `~/Downloads`. On that file:
- **Before:** the build fails with "Geometry exceeds the demo voxel budget".
- **After:** it builds in about 0.3 s using about 38 MB, with walkable floor on both levels. You can place points on either floor.

**What you'll still see:** waypoints now place, but longer routes fail with "No complete route connects these regions." With the NavMesh building, I measured how it breaks apart, roughly 14 disconnected pieces:
- the lower floor splits in two at about z = −25;
- the stairwell (near x = −12, z = −40) breaks into several small pieces;
- the upper floor is one large piece.

That's your second issue, gaps cutting off the path, and ACEB is now a real test case for it. `main` also just merged #59, which adds a tool that fills holes in scans; I'll look at it when we start that.

# Automatic deploys to not404.vodka

Every 2 minutes the server checks `main` on GitHub. When there's a new commit, it builds it and puts it live. Merging a PR into `main` is all it takes. A deploy usually finishes 3–5 minutes after the merge.

| Part | What happens | If it fails |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Website (`apps/web`) | Builds with pnpm in `/srv/not404/web-builds/<sha>`, then swaps it into `/srv/not404/web`. The previous build stays in `web.prev`. | The live site is unchanged. That commit isn't retried. |
| API (`services/api` + `apps/capture/processor`) | Only when those folders changed. Builds `/srv/not404/releases/api-<sha>`, points `api-current` at it, restarts `not404-api` and `not404-worker`, then checks that `/api/scans/public` answers 200 and `/api/users/me` answers 401. | Switches `api-current` back to the previous release and restarts. That commit isn't retried. |
| Database migrations | A commit that changes `services/api/drizzle` is **not** deployed to the API, because migrations are applied by hand (`docs/lidar-publishing.md`). The website still deploys. | Apply the migration, then `rm /var/lib/not404-deploy/api.pending`, and the next run deploys the API. |

Builds run as the unprivileged `not404-api` user. Root only swaps folders and restarts the two services. Server secrets stay in `/etc/not404/api.env`, which is read only for the API build.

## Check and control it

```sh
ssh root@155.138.139.241
journalctl -u not404-deploy -n 50          # what the last runs did
systemctl list-timers not404-deploy.timer  # when it runs next
systemctl start not404-deploy              # deploy now, without waiting
cat /var/lib/not404-deploy/{web,api}.sha   # what's live
systemctl disable --now not404-deploy.timer   # pause automatic deploys
```

The website's live version is at https://not404.vodka/VERSION.txt.

content.text:
The script can't find Open3D, the library it uses to fill the holes. `numpy` is already installed, which is why it got as far as line 182. Open3D isn't, and installing it into your current Python won't work. The tool's README says it needs **Python 3.10–3.12**, your `python` is **3.14.8**, and Open3D doesn't publish packages for 3.14.

**Fix:** run the tool under Python 3.12 in an isolated environment. On Arch the easiest way is `uv`, which downloads a 3.12 interpreter itself and leaves the system Python alone:

```sh
sudo pacman -S uv
uv run --python 3.12 --with open3d --with numpy \
  tools/scan_fill_holes.py "<input>.glb" "<output>.glb"
```

`pip install open3d` on the system Python fails in two ways: Arch blocks installing into the system Python, and there's no 3.14 build.

**Second problem:** there's no `scan.glb` in the repo root, so once Open3D loads, the script will fail on the missing file. Point it at a real scan. For ACEB Large, the copy matching the uploaded record is in Downloads:

```sh
uv run --python 3.12 --with open3d --with numpy tools/scan_fill_holes.py \
  "$HOME/Downloads/2026-11-21 2333 - 3D map.glb" "$HOME/Downloads/aceb-large-filled.glb"
```

Its README says a scan of this size takes about 3 minutes on a laptop CPU.

**How this relates to the gaps:** it only fills small cracks, up to 0.12 m (`--max-gap`), and you run it on your machine before uploading. It won't bridge large gaps, so it probably won't reconnect the ACEB pieces at z ≈ −25 or in the stairwell. Scans that are already uploaded don't change either. If you run it on ACEB, I can rebuild the NavMesh on the filled file and count how many disconnected pieces remain. That will show whether the routing fix needs to happen in the viewer.

docs/backend-plan.md:9:Spaces own one coordinate frame in metres with +Y up. Scan geometry is stored in object storage; each scan records a 16-number transform into its space. Matrix ordering and final capture format must be agreed with Krishna and Anish before real-scan integration. The current synthetic fixture uses +X right and −Z forward. Graph nodes and edges are explicit walkable data; route calculation in Arielle's viewer uses only authorized, connected spaces. A QR marker or manual selection supplies the MVP start point.
docs/backend-plan.md:11:Visibility is `private`, `unlisted`, or `public`, with `private` as the default. Public resources are discoverable; unlisted resources require an opaque link; private resources require ownership, a viewer grant, or event membership where explicitly supported. A public event or path must not expose a private space or scan merely by referencing it. Every metadata, graph and object URL request must recheck effective access server-side. Existing downloaded bytes cannot be revoked. Event rows reference spaces, paths and destinations rather than copying them. Saved paths are ordered node references and may be used outside events.

type Context = { params: Promise<{ id: string }> };
export async function GET(request: Request, context: Context) {
  const { id } = await context.params;
  return api(request, async ({ db, user }) => {
    const event = await readEvent(db, user, uuid.parse(id));
    requireOwner(signedIn(user), event.ownerId);
    const members = await db.select().from(eventMembers).where(eq(eventMembers.eventId, event.id));
    return Response.json({ members });
  });
}

}

content.content:
Visibility defaults to private; names default to `Untitled map`. The body is limited
to 400 MiB, including requests without Content-Length. Next.js proxy buffering is
set to 34 MiB so the default 10 MB buffer does not truncate valid uploads. PLY imports return 415.
A successful upload returns 201 `{id, shareId, sharePath, name, visibility}`.

Each browser import gets its own unlisted containing space. Its scan controls
public discovery and private/unlisted/public reads. Unlisted maps open signed out
from their opaque link and stay out of both scan and space discovery. Private
maps require ownership or a viewer grant. Changing visibility through
`PATCH /api/scans/:id` rechecks access on the next metadata and asset request.
The returned `id` is used for edits; `shareId` is used for guest links.
No database migration is needed; the existing visibility enum includes unlisted.

## Python integration mock

Sam owns the durable backend. The team can integrate against the local reference API now with Python 3.9+ and Make. From the repo root, run `make dev-api` in one terminal, then upload the fixture from another.

```sh
curl --fail-with-body -sS \
  -H 'X-Dev-User: demo-owner' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/octet-stream' \
  --data-binary @fixtures/venue/scene.ply \
  'http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/scans?format=ply&visibility=unlisted&name=Engineering%20building'
```

The response includes `shareId` and `sharePath`. Open `http://127.0.0.1:8001` followed by that path in another browser on the same computer. The development page links to the exact uploaded bytes. Arielle’s guest page will use the metadata and asset endpoints below to render the model.

| Request | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/scans?format=ply&visibility=unlisted&name=…` | Send raw bytes. Accepts `ply` or `glb`. Visibility defaults to `private`. `name` is optional (default `Untitled map`). Returns 201 with `{shareId, sharePath, name}`. |
| `GET /api/scans/public` | Returns `{scans: [{shareId, sharePath, name, updatedAt}]}` for public discovery, newest first. No sign-in needed. |
| `GET /api/scans/mine` | The signed-in account's own maps, newest first: `{scans: [{shareId, sharePath, name, format, visibility, viewerIds, updatedAt}]}`. 401 when signed out. |
| `GET /api/scans/shared` | Maps other accounts added the signed-in account to: `{scans: [{shareId, sharePath, name, format, visibility, owner, updatedAt}]}`, without anyone's viewer list. 401 when signed out. |
| `GET /api/shares/<shareId>` | Returns `{shareId, format, assetPath, name}` to a permitted viewer. |
| `GET /api/shares/<shareId>/asset` | Returns the uploaded file after the same access check. |
| `GET /api/shares/<shareId>/thumbnail` | The map-card picture (JPEG) after the same access check; 404 until the owner has opened the map once. |
| `PUT /api/scans/<scanId>/thumbnail` | Owner only. Saves the map-card picture: an `image/jpeg` body up to 512 KiB, stored next to the GLB as `scans/<scanId>.jpg` and deleted with the scan. |
| `PATCH /api/scans/<shareId>` | Owner sends JSON with any of `name`, `visibility` and `viewerIds`. Fields left out keep their value. `viewerIds`, when sent, is the complete replacement list. Returns `{shareId, name, visibility, viewerIds}`. |
| `DELETE /api/scans/<shareId>` | Owner only. Returns 204, removes the stored file, and every route for that share then answers 404. Anyone else gets 404. |

Names are 1–80 characters after trimming and collapsing spaces, with no control characters. Invalid names get 400. `updatedAt` is an ISO 8601 UTC time that changes on upload and on every `PATCH`.

To grant private access, send `{"visibility":"private","viewerIds":["teammate"]}` as the owner. Repeat with an empty list to revoke access. To rename, send `{"name":"Library study rooms"}`. The smoke test covers these changes, partial changes, the owner and shared lists, deletion, the raw asset URL, and unauthenticated discovery.

The mock binds to loopback, uses `X-Dev-User` to simulate an account, checks file headers, limits uploads to 400 MiB, and discards data on exit. On the hosted API derive identity from a verified session, validate the uploaded model, persist grants, and enforce visibility on every read. Use the deployed site’s origin for portable share URLs. [Architecture and data model](../../docs/architecture.md)

gh pr create --base main --head feature/share-private-maps --reviewer AryBaum --title "Let owners share private maps with people by email" --body-file - <<'EOF'
**Human owner:** Sam. **Reviewer:** Arielle (Manage map / sharing UI).

## Why
Private maps could only be opened by their owner. The access rule already existed (`scan_viewers` plus `canReadScan`, and the **Shared with me** list), but nothing let an owner add anyone, and `users` stored no email to look people up by.

## Change
**Database:** migration `0007_user_email` adds a nullable `users.email` and an index. The existing `scan_viewers` table holds the grants, so no new relationship is needed.
- **Filled automatically:** on each signed-in request, from the website's Auth0 session, which includes the email scope.
- **Verified only:** stored lower-cased, and only when Auth0 marks the email verified, so nobody can claim someone else's address and get their maps.
- **Not unique:** one person can sign in through more than one Auth0 connection.

**API (owner only):**
- `GET /api/scans/:id/viewers` returns `{viewers: [{id, displayName, email}]}`.
- `POST /api/scans/:id/viewers` with `{"email"}` adds every account with that verified email. If none has it, the response is 404 `USER_NOT_FOUND` with "Ask them to sign in to Not 404 once". The owner's own email returns 400.
- `DELETE /api/scans/:id/viewers/:userId` removes one person.
- People who can already open the map get 403; everyone else gets 404. Emails are returned only to the owner, and `/users/me` and the map lists still pick explicit fields.

**Website:** on Manage map, choosing **Private** shows **Shared users**. It lists each person's name and email with a Remove button, plus an "Add by email" form. Errors and confirmations are announced. The upload finish screen and the local mock (which has no viewer routes) show the names read-only.

## ⚠️ Deploy
The auto-deploy skips the API for commits that touch `services/api/drizzle`. **Apply `0007_user_email` to Tiger by hand**, then `rm /var/lib/not404-deploy/api.pending` (`deploy/auto/README.md`). Until then the website deploys and Shared users falls back to read-only. Existing accounts get their email the next time they use the site signed in.

## Checks
- **New API test** (`scan-viewers.test.ts`) on a disposable PostgreSQL 18 with all 8 migrations applied, not Tiger. It covers:
  - case-insensitive add;
  - two accounts with the same email both added;
  - adding twice;
  - unknown email (404) and the owner's own email (400);
  - viewer gets 403, stranger gets 404;
  - `canReadScan` and **Shared with me** before and after add and remove;
  - unverified emails never stored;
  - all three routes return 401 signed out.
- Full API suite: 65 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (as on `main`). `next build` registers both routes.
- **New browser tests** (`auth.browser.spec.ts`): add an unknown email, add one in mixed case, remove, hide and reshow on visibility change, and a read-only fallback for a server without viewer routes. `pnpm test`, `pnpm build`, `test:navmesh:browser` (10 passed) and `make check` (all three visibility modes, grants and revocation) pass.
- `auth.browser.spec.ts` › "GLB upload preserves the scan edit ID…" fails on `main` since #61 and is fixed by #63, not this PR.

**Not verified:** a real Auth0 login supplying `email_verified`, or the hosted deployment. Today all 4 production accounts have no stored email; they get it on their next signed-in visit.

**Known limit:** a grant doesn't help when the scan's own space is **private**, because `canReadScan` checks the space first. Every current map is in an unlisted or public space, so nothing is affected today. Scans from the phone pipeline placed in private spaces would need a follow-up.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

content.text:
I've done both, as two separate PRs. Neither is merged yet.

**Your database question:** the relationship already exists. The `scan_viewers` table links a map to the people allowed to open it, and private maps already let those people in and show up under **Shared with me**. What was missing is that `users` stores no email, so there was nothing to look someone up by. That needs one new column, not a new relationship.

### PR #64: Shared users on private maps (Arielle reviewing)
https://github.com/darkprince558/path-app/pull/64
- **Website:** on Manage map, choosing **Private** shows a **Shared users** section. It lists each person's name and email with a Remove button, plus an "Add by email" box.
- **Emails:** a new `users.email` column (migration `0007`). It fills in automatically when someone uses the website signed in, but only with an email Auth0 has verified. Without that check, someone could sign up with your teammate's address and be given their maps. Only the owner sees the emails.
- **API:** new owner-only routes to list, add (by email) and remove people.
- **Tests:** passed on a throwaway local database, never Tiger, including the new tests for these routes. The browser tests, build and `make check` pass too.

Three limits:
- **Sign in first:** a person can only be added after they've signed in to the website once. Today none of the 4 production accounts has an email stored; each gets one on their next signed-in visit.
- **Private spaces:** adding someone won't let them in if the map sits inside a private *space*. Every map you have today is in an unlisted or public space, so nothing is affected now; maps from the phone pipeline might need a follow-up.
- **Not tested with a real Auth0 login:** I couldn't confirm that your session actually sends the "email verified" flag.

### PR #63: upload with any visibility (Krishna reviewing)
https://github.com/darkprince558/path-app/pull/63

The forced-Private lock was added on purpose 35 minutes earlier in Krishna's map-places PR (#61), so he's the reviewer. I removed it at upload and also on Manage map. Otherwise a map uploaded as Public with no places would show a locked picker. "Next: label places" stays as a suggestion. That PR also fixes an existing upload browser test that has been failing on `main` since #61.

### Decision for you
After you merge #64, the API won't deploy until migration `0007` is applied to Tiger by hand, because the auto-deploy skips the API whenever migrations change. Until then the website still works, and Shared users shows names read-only. Do you want me to apply the migration once it's merged? It only adds a column and an index, but it writes to production, so I won't run it without your go-ahead.

Your checkout is now on `feature/share-private-maps`.

}

deploy_api() {
  local current_link current release
  current_link=$(readlink -f "$ROOT/api-current" || true)
  current=$(cat "$STATE/api.sha" 2>/dev/null || basename "$current_link" | sed 's/^api-//')
  current=$(as_builder git -C "$REPO" rev-parse --verify --quiet "$current^{commit}" || echo "")
  if [ -n "$current" ] && as_builder git -C "$REPO" diff --quiet "$current" "$NEW" -- services/api apps/capture/processor; then
    echo "$NEW" > "$STATE/api.sha"; log "api: no API changes in $SHORT"; return 0
  fi
  if [ -n "$current" ] && ! as_builder git -C "$REPO" diff --quiet "$current" "$NEW" -- services/api/drizzle; then
    echo "$NEW" > "$STATE/api.pending"
    log "api: $SHORT adds database migrations; NOT deployed. Apply them by hand, then run: rm $STATE/api.pending; echo <applied-sha> > $STATE/api.sha"
    return 0
  fi
  release="$ROOT/releases/api-$SHORT"
  log "api: building $SHORT"
  rm -rf "$release"; install -d -o "$BUILD_USER" -g "$BUILD_USER" "$release" || return 1
  as_builder sh -c "set -e; git -C '$REPO' archive '$NEW' services/api apps/capture/processor > '$release/src.tar'; tar -xf '$release/src.tar' -C '$release'; rm '$release/src.tar'" || return 1
  (cd "$release/apps/capture/processor" && as_builder npm ci --no-audit --no-fund --loglevel=error) || return 1
  (cd "$release/services/api" && as_builder npm ci --no-audit --no-fund --loglevel=error) || return 1
  (cd "$release/services/api" && set -a && . "$ENV_FILE" && set +a && runuser -u "$BUILD_USER" --preserve-environment -- env HOME=/var/lib/not404 npm run build >/dev/null)     || { log "api: build of $SHORT failed; the live API is unchanged"; echo "$NEW" > "$STATE/api.failed"; return 1; }
  local previous="$current_link"
  ln -sfn "$release" "$ROOT/api-current.new" && mv -T "$ROOT/api-current.new" "$ROOT/api-current" || return 1
  systemctl restart not404-api not404-worker || true
  if api_healthy; then
    echo "$NEW" > "$STATE/api.sha"; rm -f "$STATE/api.failed"
    log "api: live at $SHORT"
  else
    log "api: $SHORT failed its health check; rolling back to $(basename "$previous")"
    ln -sfn "$previous" "$ROOT/api-current.new" && mv -T "$ROOT/api-current.new" "$ROOT/api-current"
    systemctl restart not404-api not404-worker
    echo "$NEW" > "$STATE/api.failed"
    api_healthy && log "api: rollback healthy" || log "api: ROLLBACK ALSO UNHEALTHY, check journalctl -u not404-api"
    return 1
  fi
}

[Unit]
Description=Not 404: deploy the newest main (website and API)
Wants=network-online.target
After=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/not404-deploy
TimeoutStartSec=20min
Environment=COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT=0
Environment=NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1
not404-deploy.service
not404-deploy.sh
not404-deploy.timer
README.md
18:ROOT=/srv/not404
19:REPO=$ROOT/repo
20:STATE=/var/lib/not404-deploy
22:ENV_FILE=/etc/not404/api.env

**Roll back the website:** `mv /srv/not404/web /srv/not404/web.bad && mv /srv/not404/web.prev /srv/not404/web`.

**Roll back the API:** `ln -sfn /srv/not404/releases/api-<old-sha> /srv/not404/api-current.new && mv -T /srv/not404/api-current.new /srv/not404/api-current && systemctl restart not404-api not404-worker`.

After a manual rollback, pause the timer too, or the next new commit deploys again.

## Install (already done on the server)

```sh
install -m 755 deploy/auto/not404-deploy.sh /usr/local/bin/not404-deploy
cp deploy/auto/not404-deploy.service deploy/auto/not404-deploy.timer /etc/systemd/system/
systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl enable --now not404-deploy.timer
```

It pulls the public repository over HTTPS, so no GitHub secrets or deploy keys are needed. If the repo goes private again, add a read-only deploy key and switch `REPO_URL` to SSH.

content.text:
Both PRs are merged into `main` and the migration is applied to Tiger. The new API isn't live yet, though, and needs one step from you on the server.

**Merged**
- **#63 (any visibility at upload):** merged as `70d89f9`. The website is already running it; https://not404.vodka/VERSION.txt shows `70d89f92`.
- **#64 (Shared users):** merged as `13b4556`. It conflicted with #63 on one line in `ManageMap.tsx`. I kept both changes: the Shared users section stays and the sharing lock stays removed. With both combined, all 10 sharing browser tests pass, including the upload test that had been broken on `main`. CI passed before the merge.

**Migration applied to Tiger**
- Before running it, I confirmed Tiger's 7 recorded migrations match the repo files exactly, so only `0007` ran.
- It recorded as #8. `users.email` and its index exist, and all 4 accounts are intact. None has an email yet; each gets one on its next signed-in visit to the website.

**Why the API isn't live**
I tried to check the deploy state over SSH as root, and Claude Code's safety check blocked it. That seems right, since you hadn't asked for server access, so I stopped there. Looking at the deploy script, I found it can't release this commit on its own:
- A commit that adds a migration gets marked "pending", and the API isn't deployed.
- The README's fix, removing `api.pending`, doesn't help: the next run sees the migration change again and marks it pending again.
- The script's other suggestion, writing the commit to `api.sha`, makes it think the API is already deployed, so the new code never ships.

Right now the viewer route answers 404 on the live site. Until the API ships, Shared users shows names read-only.

On the server, this runs one deploy with the migration check switched off. The migration is already applied, so that's safe:

```sh
ssh root@155.138.139.241
systemctl stop not404-deploy.timer
rm -f /var/lib/not404-deploy/api.pending
sed 's#! as_builder git -C "$REPO" diff --quiet "$current" "$NEW" -- services/api/drizzle#false#' \
  /usr/local/bin/not404-deploy > /root/not404-deploy-once
bash /root/not404-deploy-once && journalctl -u not404-deploy -n 5 --no-pager
systemctl start not404-deploy.timer
```

Once it's live, a signed-out request to `/api/scans/<id>/viewers` should return 401 instead of 404.

Should I open a small PR that fixes the deploy script properly? After applying a migration by hand you'd write the commit to an `api.migrated` file, and the script would then deploy that commit's API instead of marking it pending again.

Your checkout is on `main`, up to date.

content.content:
| Destinations | `GET/POST /api/destinations`, `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/destinations/:id` | `{destinations: [...]}` or `{destination}`; list accepts `?spaceId=<uuid>` |
| Saved paths | `GET/POST /api/paths`, `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/paths/:id` | `{paths: [...]}` or `{path}` with ordered `waypoints` and coordinates |
| Events | `GET/POST /api/events`, `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/events/:id` | `{events: [...]}` or `{event,spaces,paths,destinations}` |
| Membership | `POST/DELETE /api/events/:id/join`, `GET /api/events/:id/members`, `DELETE /api/events/:id/members/:userId` | Join returns `{eventId,role}`; member list is organizer-only |

Successful creates return 201, deletes 204. Common errors are 400 for invalid input, 401 for missing/invalid authentication on writes, 403 for authenticated nonowners attempting to modify a visible resource, 404 for missing or inaccessible resources, and 409 for references that prevent deletion or visibility changes. The space owner creates graph nodes, edges and destinations. Both edge nodes and each destination node must be in that space; the database also enforces this. A saved path has at least two nodes, and each consecutive pair must follow a directed edge or either direction of a bidirectional edge. Public paths require public spaces.

An event links existing spaces, paths and destinations by ID. Every linked path and destination must belong to a linked space. Public events can link only public spaces and public paths. A private event may link the organizer's private resources; members who join with its invite code can then read those linked spaces, graphs and paths. The invite code appears only to the event owner. Event responses contain no scans or storage URLs. A public event or path cannot grant access to private scans.

**Human owner:** Sam. **Reviewer:** Arielle (new sidebar section and event pages in the web app).

## What it does
- **Create:** an organizer creates an event, attaches their own maps (any visibility), and shares an invite link or QR code.
- **Join:** anyone who opens the link sees a preview, signs in if needed, and joins.
- **Use:** members find the event under **Events** in the sidebar and open its maps with everything a map has (model, places, directions, approved cues). Private maps included.

## Access rule (decided with Sam)
Members can open **exactly the maps attached to the event**, nothing else.
- **New table:** `event_maps` (migration `0008`). `canReadScan` grants a member a map only if it's attached to an event they joined *and* that event's organizer owns the map.
- **Old rule kept:** "event membership never grants access to private scans" via `event_spaces` still holds, and its test in `scans.test.ts` still passes. Other maps in the same space stay private.
- **Who can attach:** only the organizer, only their own maps. Someone else's map is reported as not found, so nobody can re-share a map they don't own.
- **Taking effect:** detaching, leaving or removal applies on the next request. Deleting a map removes it from every event.
- **Invite codes:** a wrong code returns 404, like a missing event.

## API
- **New:** `GET /api/events/mine`, `POST /api/events/:id/maps` (`{scanId}`), `DELETE /api/events/:id/maps/:scanId`, and the invite preview `GET /api/events/:id/join?code=` (works signed out).
- **Changed, additively:** event `GET`/`POST`/`PATCH` now include `role` and `maps`, and the member list includes `displayName`.
- Documented in `docs/core-api.md`.

## Web
- **Sidebar:** an **Events** dropdown under Community: **Create event** first, then events you organize or joined. Phones get an **Events** tab.
- **Pages:** `/events` (list), `/events/new`, `/events/:id`, and `/events/:id/join?code=`.
  - **Organizers** get the invite link with copy and QR, add/remove maps, members with remove, and delete event.
  - **Members** get Leave event.
- **Replaced:** the old `EventView`, which listed spaces and paths; nothing in the app linked to it.
- **Robustness:** a server without `/events/mine` makes the sidebar show "No events yet" instead of crashing. A browser test caught this.

## ⚠️ Deploy
It touches `services/api/drizzle`, so the auto-deploy will hold the API: **apply `0008_event_maps` to Tiger**, then release the API by hand as we did for #64. Until then the website shows Events, but event calls fail.

## Checks
- **API, new `event-maps.test.ts`** on a disposable PostgreSQL with all 9 migrations:
  - attach (own maps only, idempotent);
  - outsider can't attach;
  - preview with wrong or missing code returns 404;
  - before and after join: the attached map opens via `canReadScan` and `readShare`, while an unattached map in the same space doesn't;
  - organizer-only `id` and invite code;
  - `mine` counts, member names, a member gets 403 on the member list;
  - detach, leave, and deleting a map.
- **Full API suite:** 67 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (as on `main`). `next build` registers every route.
- **Web, new `events.browser.spec.ts`** (run with `test:auth:browser`):
  - sidebar dropdown → create → invite link → add a map → members → delete;
  - signed-out invite preview with a sign-in link that returns to the invite;
  - signed-in join → member view → leave → access gone;
  - wrong code;
  - phone Events tab.
- `auth.browser.spec.ts` now mocks the sidebar's events call. With no session, a real 401 there signs the synthetic session out. All 15 pass.
- `pnpm test`, `pnpm build` and `make check` pass.
- `test:navmesh:browser`: 10 passed, 1 failed. "space manual and saved routes survive automatic mode" **also fails on `main` at 848b2e1**; it isn't from this PR.

**Not verified:** real Auth0 sign-in round trip through the invite link, the deployed site, a phone.

EOF

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Not 404 automatic deploy: builds the newest `main` and puts it live on not404.vodka.
# Runs every 2 minutes from not404-deploy.timer; also `systemctl start not404-deploy`.
#
# Website: builds apps/web, then swaps /srv/not404/web (previous build kept in web.prev).
# API (Sam's services/api + Anish's capture processor): builds a release in
#   /srv/not404/releases/api-<sha>, points api-current at it, restarts not404-api and
#   not404-worker, and checks the API answers. If it doesn't, it switches back.
#   A commit that changes services/api/drizzle (database migrations) is NOT deployed:
#   migrations are applied by hand (docs/lidar-publishing.md), so the API waits.
#
# Builds run as the unprivileged not404-api user; root only swaps folders and restarts.
# Logs: journalctl -u not404-deploy.   Live version: https://not404.vodka/VERSION.txt
set -euo pipefail

REPO_URL=https://github.com/darkprince558/path-app.git

The website still deploys. | Apply the migration, then `rm /var/lib/not404-deploy/api.pending`, and the next run deploys the API. |

Let the auto-deploy release the API after hand-applied migrations

A commit with migrations was held forever: removing api.pending made the next
run hold it again, and writing the SHA to api.sha (the logged advice) marked the
API as live without deploying it. Now record the applied commit in
api.migrated; that commit and any later one with the same migrations deploy.

git push -q -u origin fix/deploy-manual-migrations 2>&1 | grep -v "^remote:\|entire"; gh pr create --base main --head fix/deploy-manual-migrations --title "Let the auto-deploy release the API after hand-applied migrations" --body-file - <<'EOF'
**Human owner:** Sam (deploy).

## Problem
After a commit that adds a migration, the API was never released automatically:
- **Removing `api.pending`** (the README's advice): the next run compares against the old `api.sha` again, sees the migration change again, and holds the commit again.
- **Writing the SHA to `api.sha`** (the log line's advice): the script then thinks that commit is already live, so it skips building it.

We hit this with #64 and released it by hand.

## Fix
After applying migrations by hand, run `echo <sha> > /var/lib/not404-deploy/api.migrated && rm /var/lib/not404-deploy/api.pending`. The log line now prints this with the right SHA.
- That commit deploys, and so does any later `main` whose migrations match it.
- A newer migration is held again.
- A missing or invalid marker behaves as before.

## Checks
`bash -n`, plus `deploy_api` run on a scratch repo with the build steps stubbed. Live A → commit B adds a migration:

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| No marker | held |
| Marker B → B | builds |
| Marker B → C (same migrations, later commit) | builds |
| Marker B → D (new migration) | held |
| Marker D → D | builds |
| Live C → D, no marker | held |
| Marker is garbage → D | held |
| Live D → D | "no API changes" |

## ⚠️ Install
The server runs an installed copy. After merging: `install -m 755 deploy/auto/not404-deploy.sh /usr/local/bin/not404-deploy` (as in the README).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

content.text:
Events is built and tested as PR #66, along with a deploy-script fix as PR #67; neither is merged. Your checkout is back on an up-to-date `main`.

### PR #66: Events (Arielle reviewing)
https://github.com/darkprince558/path-app/pull/66

**What you get**
- **Sidebar:** an **Events** dropdown under Community, with **Create event** first and then the events you organize or joined. Phones get an **Events** tab.
- **Event page:**
  - Everyone in the event sees its maps and opens them like any map, with the model, places and directions.
  - The organizer also gets the invite link with a copy button and QR code, can add or remove their own maps, can see and remove members, and can delete the event.
  - Members get a Leave button.
- **Invite link:** opening it shows "Sam invited you to Open day · 3 maps", even signed out. It then asks the person to sign in, brings them back, and they join with one click.

**What already existed:** most of the backend was there: events, invite codes, join/leave and member lists. The real gap was access. Joining an event couldn't open private maps, because of your earlier rule that event membership never grants access to private scans.

**How access works now** (per map, as you chose)
- A new `event_maps` table records which maps are attached (migration `0008`).
- Members can open exactly the attached maps, whatever their visibility. Other maps in the same space stay private, so your old rule still holds and its test still passes.
- Only the organizer can attach maps, and only their own, so nobody can re-share a map they don't own.
- Leaving, removal or detaching takes effect on the next request.

**Tests:** new API tests ran on a throwaway database (the full API suite passes). New browser tests cover create, invite and join, signed-out invites, a wrong code, leave and the phone tab; the build and `make check` pass. One existing NavMesh browser test, "space manual and saved routes", fails, but it fails identically on `main` since commit `848b2e1`, so it isn't from this PR. The tests also caught a real bug: an older server without the events-list route made the sidebar crash. That's fixed. Not tested yet: a real Auth0 sign-in through an invite link, the deployed site, a phone.

### PR #67: deploy-script fix
https://github.com/darkprince558/path-app/pull/67

After applying a migration by hand, you record the commit in `/var/lib/not404-deploy/api.migrated`. The next automatic run then releases the API, and so do later commits with the same migrations. I checked 8 scenarios on a scratch repo.

### Releasing these
#66 needs the same steps as last time: merge #67 and install its script on the server, merge #66, apply `0008` to Tiger, then record the commit in `api.migrated`. With #67 in place, the deploy releases the API on its own, with no one-off script. Until the migration is applied, the website shows Events but event calls fail. Do you want me to do that whole sequence?

### Stretch goal: showing your location on the model
You're right that the current workflow can't do this. GPS doesn't work indoors, and a browser can't match its camera view to our scan. Options, cheapest first:

1. **QR "you are here" markers.** The organizer prints QR codes and pins each one to a spot on the model, the same way places are pinned. Scanning one opens the map with that spot as your start point. This fits the original plan of navigating from a QR-marked starting point, needs no new hardware, and is reliable. I'd build this first.
2. **QR plus step counting.** Start from a scanned QR code, then estimate movement from the phone's motion sensors and nudge the dot along the route. Expect it to drift a few metres per 50 m and need confirming at turns. It's fine as an "approximately here" dot.
3. **Matching the camera view to the scan.** The phone sends a camera frame, and a server matches it against the capture's keyframes to find where you're standing. That's accurate to under a metre and works anywhere in the scan, but it's a research project: a server-side matching pipeline, privacy questions about camera frames, and a few seconds per fix. Gemini can't give metric positions, so it wouldn't replace this.
4. **Native iPhone app.** Load the scan's saved ARKit map and let the phone recognise the room, which gives live tracking. It only works on iPhones, needs the app installed, and only works in the walk that captured the room.
5. **Bluetooth beacons or Wi-Fi.** Real indoor positioning, but it needs hardware in the venue and calibration. Not a fit for a hackathon.

Option 1 is a small follow-up that reuses places and routing; option 2 can be layered on top later.

content.text:
Both PRs are merged and the migration is applied, but the new API isn't live yet. Here's where things stand.

**Done**
- **Pulled `origin/main`** first. It had 3 new commits, including #65's map caching. I merged them into the events branch locally and reran the checks: typecheck, unit tests, build and all 15 browser tests pass.
- **#67 merged** (`a816199`): the deploy-script fix.
- **#66 merged** (`8733b0d`): Events.
- **Migration `0008` applied to Tiger.** I first confirmed Tiger's 8 recorded migrations match the repo's files byte for byte, so only `0008` ran. `event_maps` now exists with its key and both foreign keys, and existing data is intact: 4 users, 12 maps, 1 event. I ran it from here with the API's own migration tool against the same database; nothing needed running on the VM itself.

**Not done: installing the fixed deploy script on the server.** Claude Code's safety check blocked it. Your permission covered SSH and the migration, and it treated replacing the deploy script as more than that. The server is still on the old script, and its log shows it hasn't picked up `8733b0d` yet; the live site is still at `a816199`. On its next run the website will go live with Events, but the old script will hold the API, as before. Until the API ships, the sidebar's Events list shows "No events yet", and creating or joining an event fails. The current API answers 400 for `/api/events/mine`, and the guard I added keeps that from crashing anything.

To finish, either say "go ahead and install the deploy script and release the API", or run this yourself:

```sh
ssh root@155.138.139.241
install -m 755 /srv/not404/repo/deploy/auto/not404-deploy.sh /usr/local/bin/not404-deploy
echo 8733b0d1e42788871d9af7f0273998bb22994611 > /var/lib/not404-deploy/api.migrated
rm -f /var/lib/not404-deploy/api.pending
systemctl start not404-deploy && journalctl -u not404-deploy -n 5 -o cat --no-pager
```

The server's own copy of the repo already has the fixed script, because it fetched `a816199`. The marker tells it `0008` is applied, so it releases `8733b0d` and any later commit with the same migrations. content.text:
Events is fully live: the website and API are both running `8733b0d`, and migration `0008` is on Tiger.

**What I did on the server**
- Installed the fixed deploy script, after confirming it's identical to `main`. The old one is backed up at `/root/not404-deploy.bak`.
- Recorded `8733b0d` in `api.migrated` and cleared `api.pending`.
- Started a deploy. The new script released the API by itself, with no workaround this time: it built and switched to the new release, restarted the API and worker, and passed its own health checks. The auto-deploy timer, API and worker are all running.

**Checks from outside**
- `/api/events/mine` now answers 401 when signed out; it answered 400 before the release.
- An invite preview with a wrong code returns 404.
- The new maps route exists; a GET returns 405 because it only accepts POST.
- The invite page loads.
- `/api/scans/public` returns 200 and `/api/users/me` returns 401, as before.

**Still to try with real accounts:** create an event, add a map, then open the invite link in another browser signed in as someone else and join. That person should see the map under **Events** in their sidebar, including a Private one. Nobody has tested that round trip with real Auth0 sign-in yet.

**Next time a PR adds a migration:** the deploy log line now names the right commit. After applying the migration, run `echo <sha> > /var/lib/not404-deploy/api.migrated && rm /var/lib/not404-deploy/api.pending` and the next automatic run releases the API.

Still open from earlier: routing across gaps on ACEB, and the QR "you are here" markers if you want to take on the location idea.

The tool rebuilds the whole surface with Poisson reconstruction, and its default `--depth 10` divides the longest side into 1,024 cells. Over 281 m, that's about 27 cm per cell, while the scan itself was fused at 4 cm. The default was tuned on a single hallway; on a building this size it produces a coarse, blobby version. The "Found bad data" warning is unrelated: one vertex has a zero-length normal, and it's harmless.

**What's running now:** the first command again with `--depth 12`, which gives about 7 cm cells, written to `~/Downloads/full_preview/scan-filled.glb`. I'm tracking its time and peak memory. Based on that, I'll rerun the `--levels` version at depth 12, or at 13 (about 3.4 cm, matching the scan's own resolution) if memory allows. I renamed the depth-10 outputs to `scan-filled-depth10.glb` and `scan-best-depth10.glb`, so you can compare them.

**For later:** the tool could pick the depth from the scan's size and fusion resolution instead of a fixed 10, so large walks get the right detail by default. That's a small change to `tools/scan_fill_holes.py` if you want it.

content.text:
Both runs are done, and both files are good to view and upload. But neither this scan nor the originals can use automatic routing yet, because the viewer's size limits block it.

**Results** (Poisson `--depth 12`, about 7 cm detail)

| File | Triangles | Size | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Preview.glb` (input) | 7.5M | 199 MB | |
| `scan-filled.glb` | 2.25M | 56.5 MB | holes filled, 371 junk pieces removed, soft shadows baked |
| `scan-best.glb` | 2.25M | 56.5 MB | the same, plus `--levels`: colours stretched from 0–0.82 to the full range |

Both are in `~/Downloads/full_preview/`. Each took about 22 seconds and about 2.2 GB of memory, using a throwaway `uv` environment (Python 3.12, Open3D 0.20). Nothing was installed system-wide.

**Two things to know**

1. **I didn't run exactly what you typed.** With the tool's default `--depth 10`, both runs finished in 6 seconds with only 117k triangles. This walk is 129 m × 281 m, so depth 10 means about 27 cm of detail, a blurry version of the building. Those files are still there as `scan-filled-depth10.glb` and `scan-best-depth10.glb`. I didn't go to depth 13: it would roughly match the scan's 4 cm fusion, but the result would be bigger than the original.

2. **Routing won't work on this scan, original or filled.** I ran all three through the viewer's GLB check, which they pass; the app will treat them as phone scans. Then I tried building the NavMesh, and it fails on two of the viewer's size limits:
   - **Triangles:** the outputs have 2.25M; the limit is 2M. The original fails an earlier limit, on vertices.
   - **Footprint:** even under 2M triangles, 129 × 281 m is about 3.6M grid cells, over the 2M-cell limit.

   So simplifying the file won't be enough. Large multi-walk buildings need the NavMesh built in tiles, or at a coarser grid. That fits naturally with the routing-gaps work.

gh pr create --base main --head feature/explore-model --reviewer AryBaum --title "Walk inside scans like Street View, and move around maps like a map" --body-file - <<'EOF'
**Human owner:** Sam. **Reviewer:** Arielle (viewer controls and layout).

## Why
In the 3D view you could only spin and zoom, so you couldn't actually get to every part of a scan, especially the 129 × 281 m Hack Western DEMO.

## What changes
**Overview, map style**
- Drag pans across the ground. Right-drag or two fingers turn and tilt.
- The wheel zooms toward the cursor, and the arrow keys pan.
- The hints in the guest and space views are updated to match.

**Walk inside** (person button, top right; bottom right on phones)
- **Getting in:** drag the person onto the model, like Street View, or press it and click or tap a spot. Enter drops in at the centre, for keyboard users.
- **Moving:** you stand at 1.6 m eye height. Drag to look around. W A S D or the arrows walk, Shift runs, the wheel steps, and a click or tap on the floor glides you there.
- **Physics:** you follow floors and steps, stop 35 cm before walls, and keep your height over holes in the scan.
- **Leaving:** Esc, **Back to overview**, or **Reset view** returns you to exactly where you were above.
- **While walking:** walls show at full height, and the previous wall cut comes back on exit. The route card folds to its status line. Double-clicking to set route points still works inside.

**Opening view** (`lib/framing.ts`, shared with the map-card picture)
- Frames the bulk of the scan instead of its bounding sphere.
- Turns so the long side runs across a wide screen, or up a phone.
- The DEMO goes from a small zigzag in one corner to filling the view.

**Speed** (`three-mesh-bvh` 0.8.3, the version drei already installs)
- A BVH index is built about a second after the model appears: about 0.7 s for the DEMO.
- One ray on the DEMO drops from about 100 ms to microseconds, and a walking step costs 0.02 ms. Double-click picking on big scans gets snappier too.
- The index mode leaves the GLB's index untouched. The wall-cut click filter wraps the fast raycast, because the fast version is installed on `Mesh.prototype` before scans are prepared.

## Checks
- **Unit** (`tests/walk.test.ts`, in `pnpm test`): floor finding over holes, stopping at walls, climbing a 20 cm step, dropping on a wall lands on the floor below, heading/direction round trip.
- **Browser** (`scan-navigation.browser.spec.ts`):
  - press → a miss says "No floor there" → drop → look → walk → Esc;
  - drag the person in → Reset view;
  - a plain drag pans.
  - The point-picking helpers now use the same `overviewPose` as the viewer.
  - Each walk test passed 8 times in a row. The first version was flaky because the canvas was measured at its 300 × 150 default size.
- `test:navmesh:browser`: 14 passed, including "space manual and saved routes", which fails on `main`. `test:auth:browser`: 15 passed; one events test failed once in a full run and passed 6/6 alone, likely a cold Vite compile. `pnpm test`, `pnpm build` and `make check` pass.
- **Real DEMO GLB** (local copy, not committed) in headless Chromium on the laptop's AMD GPU, with screenshots reviewed at desktop and phone size, by mouse and by touch tap:
  - the model appears in about 1.6 s and dropping in takes about 0.2 s;
  - walking, looking and returning all worked.
  - That run tuned the floor detection: the DEMO's bumpy floor triangles tilt up to |n.y| 0.4–0.6, so faces with |n.y| ≥ 0.35 count as floor; walls are almost all under 0.2.

**Not verified:** a real phone, and the deployed site. Routing on the DEMO needs #68 as well.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

content.text:
I built both parts as two PRs, ready to merge; neither is merged yet. CI passes on both, they combine cleanly, and neither needs a migration, so the auto-deploy will ship them on its own once merged.

### Main priority: getting around the model (PR #69)
https://github.com/darkprince558/path-app/pull/69

**Map-style movement**
- Drag moves you across the ground, like Google Maps.
- Right-drag or two fingers turn and tilt.
- The scroll wheel zooms toward wherever the cursor is, and the arrow keys pan.

**"Walk inside", Street View style**
- **Getting in:** drag the person button onto any corridor, or press it and then click or tap a spot.
- **Moving:** you stand at eye height. Drag to look around. W A S D or the arrow keys walk, Shift runs, and clicking or tapping the floor glides you there.
- **Behaviour:** you follow floors and steps, stop before walls, and don't fall through holes in the scan. Walls show at full height while you're inside.
- **Leaving:** Esc or **Back to overview** returns you to exactly where you were above.

**A better starting view.** The DEMO used to sit small in one corner. The opening view now frames the building itself, long side across the screen.

**Speed.** On a scan this size, finding what's under the mouse took about 100 ms per click. A one-time index built about a second after load (using a library the 3D toolkit already installs) makes it effectively instant, which also speeds up double-click route picking.

I tested it on the actual DEMO file in a browser on your laptop's GPU and checked the screenshots, at desktop size and at phone size with touch. That run turned up two real problems, both fixed:
- The DEMO's floor is bumpy enough that dropping in failed to find the floor.
- On phones, the route card covered the Walk button. It now sits bottom-right on phones, and the route card folds while you walk.

### Auto-routing on the huge model (PR #68)
https://github.com/darkprince558/path-app/pull/68

**The cause:** routing gave up on the DEMO for two reasons. It has 2.25M triangles against a 2M limit, and its 129 × 281 m footprint is too many cells at the fixed 10 cm grid.

**The fix:** big scans now use a coarser grid (15 cm for the DEMO); rooms stay at 10 cm. The DEMO now builds its routing in about 1.3 s, with routes up to 158 m across the building.

**Remaining limit:** about a third of the floor is cut off into islands by gaps in the scan, so some start/end pairs still say "No complete route". That's the gaps fix from earlier, and it's the natural next step.

### Before the demo
- **Not tested on a real phone yet.** Building the routing on a phone may take a few seconds.
- **Inside views look soft:** the scan's colour detail is about 7 cm. Seeing hallways from inside still works well; a sharper scan would look much better.
- **Reviews:** I requested Arielle's review on both, since it's her viewer.
- **Unrelated test flake:** one events browser test failed once in a full run and passed 6 times in a row on its own. It doesn't affect these PRs.

Do you want me to merge both now, so the auto-deploy puts them on not404.vodka?
